messages:
miriam-cs: Heads-up: customer T-512 reporting sudden throughput drop on their Dedicated pool (pool-id: dp-78). Their app went from ~12k tokens/s to ~2k tokens/s around 09:12 UTC. They see increased 500s and sporadic 429s. Ticket CS-3245 opened.

liz-support: Customer says latency for simple chat completions jumped from 80ms -> 700ms p95, and some requests are failing with body: `{ "error": "internal_server_error" }`. They've pasted a sample request and token.

ajay-runtime: Thanks — can you paste sample request + headers (no secrets) and which model variant? Also, which pool (dp-78) size?

liz-support: Sample (redacted):
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer redacted
{
  "model": "redwood-4x-large-q",
  "input": "long prompt with multiple examples (~1500 tokens)",
  "max_tokens": 512
}
```
They confirmed pool dp-78 is 8xA100, reserved.

sam-sre: I pulled infra metrics for dp-78 between 09:00-09:30 UTC:
- queue_depth spiked from 20 -> 120
- batch_size_histogram shifted: mode 2-4 requests, previously 8-12
- prefill_rate increased by 4x (more small prefill-only requests)
- kv_cache_hit dropped from 98% -> 73%
Logs show many tiny microbatches and longer per-request compute times.

ajay-runtime: Sounds like batching efficiency collapse. Two quick hypotheses: noisy tenant generating many short requests causing pack-skew, or a scheduler change rolled out to reduce tail latency but lowered packing (we shipped quantum tweak last night).

miriam-cs: Customer says they didn't change traffic pattern, but they did ramp up a feature that sends longer prompts (more prefixes). Could that change effective max_batch_tokens and cause fragmentation?

ajay-runtime: Yes — longer sequence lengths can reduce batch occupancy because of token-limiting per-batch. If batcher enforces max_batch_tokens=2048, a few long requests will truncate batch packing and force small batches. Combined with increased prefill-only calls (KV misses) this explains the throughput drop.

ops-oncall: Deploy bot shows a config change at 03:10 UTC: `scheduler.quantum_ms` reduced from 12 -> 6 in canary for 25% of clusters. dp-78 was in canary group.

ajay-runtime: Ah — smaller quantum lowers latency for singletons but often reduces coalescing time window. With longer inputs we lose packing and hit max_batch_tokens earlier. That matches the pattern.

liz-support: Customer also reported intermittent 401s before errors — could be auth service timeouts; billing is concerned too (saw token count spike). Billing-bot requested hold until we confirm root cause.

billing-bot: Placing invoice hold check for CS-3245 flagged until engineering confirms anomalies are infra-related. Please escalate if customer needs credits.

sam-sre: Repro plan I ran: synthetic load with mix 80% short (50 tokens) requests and 20% long (1500 tokens) to dp-78 with current scheduler.quantum_ms=6 vs old 12. Results:
- quantum=6: average batch_size dropped 55%, throughput dropped 62%
- quantum=12: batch_size stable, throughput normal
Logs: `batcher: packed_tokens=1900/2048, microbatches=18, prefill_only=34` for quantum=6 run.

ajay-runtime: Repro confirmed. Quick mitigations:
1) Roll back scheduler.quantum_ms to 12 for dp-78 canary nodes (temp).
2) Increase max_batch_tokens to 4096 for affected pools to allow larger pack before cut.
3) Enable tenant-level routing to fallback model variant with lower max_input_length for this customer while we remediate.
4) Ask product if we want different default canary config for Dedicated pools.

miriam-cs: Customer requested immediate fix. Which of the mitigations can we do without downtime?

ops-oncall: We can patch scheduler value via feature flag toggle per-node; no full deploy. I'll target dp-78 pool and flip back to 12 for the canary subset now.

deploy-bot: Feature-flag toggle applied to 6 nodes in dp-78 canary at 09:47 UTC.

sam-sre: After toggle: queue_depth normalizing, batch_size histogram moving back toward 8-12, throughput recovered to ~10k tokens/s within 4 minutes. KV hit bouncing back.

liz-support: Customer confirms latency improving and errors subsiding. They still want a postmortem and steps to avoid recurrence.

ajay-runtime: Action items:
- (ajay) Run retrospective to decide canary defaults for Dedicated pools (quantum_ms 12 vs 6) and document tradeoffs.
- (sam) Generate metrics dump for dp-78: batch_size_histogram, pack_skew, kv_cache_hit, prefill_rate, queue_depth, autoscale_events. Attach to CS-3245.
- (ops-oncall) Add a healthcheck alert for batch_size_mode drop >40% vs baseline.
- (miriam) Coordinate customer comms and share ETA for permanent fix.
- (product) Evaluate whether default max_batch_tokens should be higher for dedicated customers with long inputs.

sam-sre: Logs and repro artifacts attached to the ticket. Key snippet from batcher logs: 
```
[09:35:12] batcher.INFO pool=dp-78 packed_tokens=1760 max_batch_tokens=2048 requests=3 pack_skew=0.71 prefill_only=29
[09:35:13] batcher.INFO pool=dp-78 packed_tokens=420 max_batch_tokens=2048 requests=2 pack_skew=0.20 prefill_only=60
```

miriam-cs: Also flagged to check if billing spike correlates to KV cache drops (more re-compute -> more tokens billed). Sam, can you correlate token count delta?

sam-sre: On it. Preliminary: token-usage jumped ~18% during window; looks correlated to longer inputs + retry/recompute.

billing-bot: Noted. Hold remains until CS confirms resolution.

ajay-runtime: Longer-term fixes: smarter batcher heuristics that adapt quantum based on load shape, tenant-aware packer, and a cap on prefill-only weight so it doesn't starve full-generation batching. I'll open RFC.

miriam-cs: Great — please keep CS looped. Marking this resolved for now after the rollback and customer confirmation. Will leave ticket open until postmortem. :white_check_mark:

liz-support: Customer says they appreciate fast response. Closing escalation for now.

ops-oncall: Monitoring dp-78 closely for 24h and will escalate if regression.

deploy-bot: Canary toggle history: `scheduler.quantum_ms` set -> 6 at 03:10, reverted -> 12 at 09:47.

miriam-cs: Thanks team.
